title: sync
description: One sync run: what it re-listed, what it stored, and why it stopped. Since #232 this is the only command that pulls data from Strava — it drains missing streams paced against Strava's limits and stops on the per-run read budget, so a first run on a fresh install may need repeating. Read `resumable` to decide.

streams_fetched.description: stream rows STORED this run. Not reads spent: a read whose body will not decode stores nothing and is counted in streams_skipped, and a 404 stores an empty marker rather than streams

streams_skipped.description: reads whose body would not decode as UTF-8. Nothing was stored, so these stay pending and retry next run. A value that repeats across runs means the data is unreadable rather than merely late

pending_streams.description: activities still without any streams row after this run. An activity Strava has no streams for does NOT count: its 404 stores an empty marker, which retires it permanently

stopped.description: Why the run ended. `complete` = the stream queue emptied; `budget_reached` = the run filled Strava's 15-minute read window; `rate_limited` = Strava returned 429 on a STREAM read; `daily_cap_reached` = stride's own count of today's reads reached Strava's daily allowance, which also covers the PRE-FLIGHT refusal where no request was made at all; `list_rate_limited` = Strava returned 429 on the ACTIVITY LIST, so the listing is incomplete and nothing was pruned (#235); `list_daily_cap_reached` = the ACTIVITY LIST was refused AND the day is already spent, so the listing is incomplete AND the remedy is tomorrow. The REMEDIES differ and that is the point of the distinction: `budget_reached`, `rate_limited` and `list_rate_limited` all clear when the 15-minute window rolls over, while `daily_cap_reached` and `list_daily_cap_reached` clear at UTC midnight — advising ~15 minutes there is an instruction that cannot succeed (#246). All six arrive in a SUCCESS envelope at exit 0. Do not discriminate on this token against the `rate_limited` ERROR code, which is a different thing in a different envelope shape — discriminate on the envelope. The two `list_*` tokens are the ones that mean ROWS ARE MISSING: `synced` and `pruned` describe a partial run. An earlier version folded the list-plus-spent-day case into `daily_cap_reached` and documented the lost fact here as acceptable — it was not, because the human surface then printed nothing at all, and the separate token is what carries it.

resumable.description: Whether anything is still missing, so the run should be repeated. Usually `pending_streams > 0`, re-measured from the database in every arm. It is also true when `stopped` is `list_rate_limited` or `list_daily_cap_reached` even with an empty queue, because what was left undone there is the LISTING, not the stream backlog — a run refused on page one has nothing pending and absolutely must be repeated. And true for `daily_cap_reached` reached through the pre-flight refusal, where no request was made at all: an empty queue there describes a run that never looked, not a queue that is genuinely drained.
